tier_reason: The README's Criterion output compares geo-index construction and search against rstar::RTree::bulk_load, and the code is public (benches/rtree.rs reading benches/bounds.raw). No CPU, rustc version or flags are stated (Cargo.toml has no profile override), so it is first-party with partial methodology: C.

corrections.stars_or_usage: 200 stars, 18 forks; used under the hood in geoarrow-rs (per the README)
corrections.caveats: The author says it is just one benchmark and recommends benchmarking on your own data. Hardware, dataset size and compiler settings are not stated. A static packed index is compared against a dynamic R-tree's bulk load, which is not like-for-like on features (rstar supports updates). Search is one fixed bounding-box query (-112.007, 40.634, -111.921, 40.694) on one dataset, so the 33% figure rests on one query; the bench does assert that both return the same result count. The rstar construction closure clones the input Vec (rect_vec.to_vec()) inside the timed loop, while geo-index builds from a borrowed slice, which adds a copy to rstar's time. The rstar dev-dependency is 0.12. The bench labels geo-index runs 'flatbush' because the tree is a Rust port of mourner's flatbush and kdbush layouts. Derived from page data: construction 1.97x, search 1.32x.

notes: Every number matches the README Benchmarks section. Metadata from github.com: MIT OR Apache-2.0 (Cargo.toml), 200 stars, 100 commits, last commit 2026-09-15 (v0.4.0), not a fork or archived. geo-index ports the flatbush/kdbush memory layout, and KDBush (JS) is in this same wave. It is a separate implementation in another language, not a wrapper, so I did not file it as a duplicate.

tier_reason: The README's 'Speed comparison' section gives first-party `time` wall-clock figures for hob3l against OpenSCAD's CGAL 3D CSG rendering on four models. It states no hardware, compiler, flags or OpenSCAD version, and has no benchmark script. With unstated flags and gains above 50x, the cap is C.

corrections.caveats: Wall-clock `time` figures on unspecified hardware and flags, against an unstated OpenSCAD version. The speedups above 50x come from a different algorithm (slice first, then 2D booleans) with layered output, so they are not like-for-like with CGAL mesh booleans; the README shows the layered STL and says the final slicer result is the same. The baseline is OpenSCAD's CGAL rendering path, not CGAL used directly, and OpenSCAD's newer Manifold backend is not compared. The 85x uselessbox figure includes writing a 23 MB STL (loading and converting alone take 0.23 s). Only a subset of SCAD is read, so full SCAD needs OpenSCAD as a preprocessor. The author admits memory leaks ('Memory management has leaks. I admit I don't care enough'). The core 2D library was fuzzed with afl. Last commit June 2024.

notes: All four timings in the record match the README verbatim (45.208 s vs 0.824 s, 2m42s vs 1.24 s, 53.433 s vs 0.610 s, 4m30.198s vs 0.748 s). Metadata from github.com: GPL-3.0 (LICENSE file), 265 stars, 17 forks, 341 commits, last commit 2024-06-23, so stale is right. Shortcoming worth recording: the author admits memory leaks.

It gives no workload, hardware or Node version. kdbush's bench.js times kdbush alone (1M Uint32 points, 10,000 bbox and radius queries) and publishes no results. Numbers without methodology: C.

corrections.caveats: The 5-8x figure is a one-line claim in RBush's README, written by the author of both libraries, with no workload, hardware or code reference. kdbush's bench.js times only kdbush (no RBush run) and publishes no numbers. The comparison is against a JavaScript R-tree, not a native library. KDBush is static and points-only, while RBush is dynamic and indexes rectangles.

notes: Claim text verified verbatim in the RBush README; the KDBush README says only 'Faster indexing and search, with lower memory footprint' compared with RBush.
